name: Thin Red Line
approach: From Highway 20 hairpin curve on east side of Washington Pass, locate small pond on south side of road; trailhead pullout on north side of highway; follow climbers' path marked with cairns from pond eastward into forest

approach_variants.name: The hairpin pond pullout and the cairned East Face path, then right of Liberty Crack
approach_variants.notes: From the Highway 20 hairpin curve on the east side of Washington Pass, locate the small pond on the south side of the road; the pullout is on the north side of the highway. Follow the cairned climbers' path from the pond eastward into forest and up to the East Face talus. Note that this route's stored trailhead coordinate does not agree with the one every other East Face route on this peak carries. Use the pond and the hairpin, not a stored point.
hazards: A start that has to be sighted from a distance rather than found along the base
Snow travel at the base into early summer
Several route starts within a short distance of each other on the same wall
A summit descent that strands you on the opposite side of the mountain from your car
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The route is climber's right of Liberty Crack, and the published method for finding it is to work downward from the features above rather than along the base. Look climber's right of Liberty Crack and connect the line down from the features higher on the wall. Some mellow snow travel is usually necessary to reach the base.

So this is the one east face route whose start is honestly described as a sighting problem, and that is worth knowing before the cloud comes down. Fix the line from the talus while you can see the wall. If you cannot see the wall, you cannot locate this start by walking the base, and no description will change that.

What you can do without a view is bound it, because the order along the base is known. Left to right: Freedom Rider about 100 ft left of Liberty Crack, Liberty Crack, Freedom or Death just right of it on a leftward-trending ramp with bolts above, Thin Red Line, Liberty and Injustice for All about 10 m right of Thin Red Line, Live Free or Die, and the Independence Route at the far right or north edge of the face beneath a red roof and alcove called the Baer Ceiling about 85 m up.

So: if you are standing at a leftward-trending ramp with bolts above it, you are one route left, on Freedom or Death. If you can see a red roof about 85 M above you, you have walked all the way right to the Independence Route.

The descent decides which car you end at, and this route has both options: from the top of the route near M&M Ledge, work climber's left to good bolts and make four double-rope rappels essentially to the ground at the base of the East Face, returning to your pack and the East Face approach. If you instead continue to the true summit and take the standard Liberty Bell notch descent, you finish on the west side of the mountain and need a shuttle or a road walk back.

waypoints.name: SR-20 Hairpin / Pond Pullout (east of Washington Pass)
waypoints.note: Roadside pullout on the north side of SR-20 at the hairpin turn east of Washington Pass, beside a small pond; the East Face climbers' path starts here.
waypoints.directions: Drive Highway 20 to the hairpin curve on the east side of Washington Pass and look for the small pond on the south side of the road; the pullout you want is on the north side of the highway, at about 5,200 ft. Park there and pick up the cairned climbers' path leaving the pond, which runs east into the forest and up to the East Face talus. The season for this line is roughly June through September.

waypoints.name: Sustained thin-crack pitches
waypoints.note: Sustained thin finger and hand cracks at 5.10-5.11 on excellent but highly exposed rock; retreating typically means leaving gear behind.
waypoints.directions: From the east end of the pond, follow the cairned climbers' path as it climbs steeply through forest to the talus and snow below the East Face. The start is right of Liberty Crack and is best picked out from the talus by tracing the line down from features higher on the wall; climb the lower pitches to the sustained corner and thin-crack pitches.

waypoints.name: Liberty Bell summit
waypoints.note: Grade IV outing tops out on the true summit; from the summit descend via the standard Beckey Route rappels/downclimb into the gully (most parties instead rappel the East Face from M&M Ledge without topping out).
waypoints.directions: Above the crux corners, continue up the crack pitches to M&M Ledge, then easier corners and ledges on the upper apron, and finish with easy scrambling to the true summit.
